claims.claim: Magic must be scarce; three wishes make a tale, infinite wishes make none.
claims.quote: an infinite number of wishes is no story at all

claims.claim: Determine coinage and the value of money and keep it consistent through the book.
claims.quote: Determine coinage and value of money

claims.claim: Research economy and geography: a tiny village will not support an artisan specialising in doorknockers.

claims.feature: food constrained by technology, geography, climate
claims.claim: A meal must be believable for the technology level, geography and climate, and such details fall naturally into the tale.
claims.source: Fran Wilde, Cooking the Books guest post (2014)
claims.quote: the technology level, the geography and climate

claims.claim: Status registers in the ordinary: food served in the kitchen was warmer than food served in the hall.
claims.source: Fran Wilde, Cooking the Books guest post (2014)
claims.quote: warmer than that served in the hall

claims.claim: A character on the frontier has a limited menu, and the constraint is listed item by item.
claims.source: Fran Wilde, Cooking the Books guest post (2014)
claims.quote: No flour, no sugar, no milk, cream or butter

claims.feature: magic paid for in the body
claims.claim: The whole saga grew from asking what if magic were addictive and degenerative, so that power is paid for physically.
Magic that everybody can do becomes commonplace technology; scarcity keeps it magic.
claims.quote: any sufficiently common magic is technology

claims.claim: Violence is written to be horrifying and ugly, never lascivious, and rape as a haunting that never fully leaves.
claims.quote: how horrifying and ugly violence is

claims.claim: Once a story goes somewhere she does not turn back or undo it with an it-was-all-a-dream.
claims.quote: Follow the story, wherever it goes

claims.claim: When a character makes a stupid decision the writer is stuck with it and must write the consequence.
What happens to a character changes her permanently, and a character not shaped by her experiences makes those experiences pointless to write.
claims.quote: The things that happen to us change us

claims.claim: Physical damage must leave aftermath, bruises, blood, limping, vomiting, because a good character does not protect anyone from a concussion.
claims.quote: no one limps or throws up in the corner

claims.feature: product of what has been done to us
claims.claim: Characters become the product of what has been done to them, or for them.
claims.quote: the product of what has been done to us

claims.claim: Characters step onto the stage unplanned and are allowed their own ideas about the story; the Fool was outlined as a minor character.
claims.quote: some characters just have their own ideas about the story
